editorial: The best time depends on which version of Salar de Uyuni you want.

seasons.title: July to October
editorial: This is the drier period and our preferred version. We visited in late October and saw the vast white salt crust at its best, while residual water in places still produced the mirror effect.
The cactus islands—especially Incahuasi—were one of our favourite parts of the day and may be harder to reach when water levels rise.

seasons.title: January to March
editorial: The wet season creates the giant mirror you have seen in photographs. If that reflection is the dream, this is the period to target, accepting that flooding can limit access to parts of the flats.

seasons.title: Shoulder Months
editorial: The awkward periods are when there may be enough water to interfere with access but not enough to create the full mirror. If Uyuni is the sole reason for travelling to Bolivia, optimise the trip around the salt rather than around slightly cheaper flights.
